question.text: Two metallic rings $A$ and $B$, identical in shape and size but having different resistivities $\rho_A$ and $\rho_B$, are kept on top of two identical solenoids as shown in the figure. When current $I$ is switched on in both the solenoids in identical manner, the rings $A$ and $B$ jump to heights $h_A$ and $h_B$, respectively, with $h_A>h_B$. The possible relation(s) between their resistivities and their masses $m_A$ and $m_B$ is(are)

solution.text:
Induced emf $e=-\frac{d \phi}{d t}$. For identical rings induced emf will be same. But currents will be different. Given $h_A>h_B$. Hence, $v_A>v_B$ as $\left(h=\frac{v^2}{2 g}\right)$.
If $\rho_A>\rho_B$, then, $I_A < I_B$. In this case given condition can be fulfilled if $m_A < m_B$.
If $\rho_A < \rho_B$, then $I_A>I_B$. In this case given condition can be fulfilled of $m_A \leq m_B$.
